title: Conceptual and Video Art
welcome_lead: The idea is the work; the screen is the surface.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: conceptual art, video art, and contemporary moving image.
final_note: When the idea is the machine that makes the art.

concepts.def: Practice in which idea takes precedence over object.
Time-based art using moving image, post-1965.
American video artist (1951-2024), large-scale slow-motion projections.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sol LeWitt's Paragraphs on Conceptual Art (1967) declared 'the idea becomes a machine that makes the art'. Execution could be delegated; the concept was primary.
Nam June Paik (1932-2006) used the Sony Portapak (1965) to make the first widely circulated artist video tapes. His TV-sculptures and installations defined the medium for decades.

Bill Viola's slow-motion HD video projections — figures emerging from water, faces in extreme emotion — return video art to questions of mortality and the sublime, exhibited in cathedrals and museums alike.
